app.title: Diabetes Risk Checker
app.subtitle: SDG 3: Good Health & Well-being — free, early diabetes screening with machine learning
app.no_model: No trained model found. Run `{cmd}` first, then reload this page.
app.disclaimer: ⚠️ This is a screening tool for awareness, not a medical diagnosis. Only a blood test (HbA1c, fasting glucose or OGTT) can diagnose diabetes.
quick.intro: Answer 14 simple questions — no blood test or lab report needed. Takes about one minute.
detailed.intro: Use this if you have recent lab results, especially a 2-hour glucose tolerance test. Fields you haven't had measured can be left as **not measured**.
q.genhlth: In general, how would you rate your health?
q.highbp: Has a doctor or health worker ever told you that you have high blood pressure?
q.highchol: Has a doctor ever told you that your cholesterol is high?
q.activity: Any exercise or physical activity in the past month (apart from your job)?
q.fruits: Do you eat fruit at least once a day?
q.veggies: Do you eat vegetables at least once a day?
q.smoker: Have you smoked at least 100 cigarettes or bidis in your life?
q.alcohol_help: Men: more than 14 drinks a week. Women: more than 7 drinks a week.
q.stroke: Have you ever had a stroke?
q.heart: Have you ever had heart disease or a heart attack?
q.diffwalk: Do you have serious difficulty walking or climbing stairs?
c.age_help: The model was trained on women aged 21–81.
c.glucose_help: Plasma glucose 2 hours into an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). Normal < 140, prediabetes 140–199, diabetes ≥ 200. A fasting reading is lower and will under-estimate risk.
c.skin_known: I know my triceps skin-fold thickness
c.out_of_range: Some readings are outside the range the model was trained on, so the estimate is less certain — but they are a reason to see a doctor.
res.risk_survey: Estimated chance of diabetes or prediabetes
band.low.msg: Low risk — keep up a healthy lifestyle and re-check every 2–3 years.
band.moderate.msg: Moderate risk — a confirmatory blood test (HbA1c or fasting glucose) is recommended, along with the lifestyle steps below.
band.high.msg: High risk — please see a doctor soon for an HbA1c or fasting blood glucose test.
res.no_drivers: Your answers are close to those of a typical person, so no single factor stands out.
res.axis: Change in risk vs. a typical person (% points)
res.drivers_caption: Each bar shows how your risk would change if that one answer were replaced by the most typical answer in the dataset. Unknown answers are skipped.
res.download: Download summary to show your doctor
sum.title: Diabetes risk screening — {date}
tip.glucose_diabetes: Your 2-hour glucose is in the **diabetes range (≥ 200 mg/dL)**. Please see a doctor promptly.
tip.glucose_igt: Your 2-hour glucose suggests **prediabetes (140–199 mg/dL)** — this is reversible with diet and activity.
tip.diastolic_high: A diastolic pressure of 80 mm Hg or more counts as high blood pressure — reduce salt and get it checked, as it adds to diabetes risk.
tip.family_history: Diabetes runs in your family — tell your doctor which relatives have it, and get your sugar checked every year.
tip.bmi_obese: Your BMI is {bmi} (obese range, 30 or more). Losing even **5–7% of body weight** cut diabetes risk by more than half in prevention trials.
tip.bmi_overweight: Your BMI is {bmi}. For South Asians, a BMI of 23 or more already raises diabetes risk — aim for **150 minutes of brisk activity a week**.
tip.get_checked: You haven't had your blood pressure or cholesterol checked. A BP check is free at any PHC or health camp — it also makes this estimate more accurate.
tip.bp_known: High blood pressure and diabetes often go together. Take prescribed medicines regularly, cut down on salt, and check your sugar once a year.
tip.activity: Aim for **30 minutes of brisk walking, 5 days a week** — regular activity lowers diabetes risk substantially.
tip.diet: Eat fruit and vegetables every day, and swap white rice, maida and sugary drinks for whole grains, millets and pulses.
tip.tobacco: Tobacco raises diabetes risk. For free help to quit, call the National Tobacco Quitline: **1800-11-2356**.
tip.alcohol: Heavy drinking harms the pancreas and liver — cutting down lowers your risk.
tip.general_health: You rated your health as fair or poor. Please see a doctor for a general check-up, including a blood sugar test.
tip.ncd_screening: Adults aged 30+ can get **free diabetes and blood-pressure screening** at government health centres (Ayushman Arogya Mandir / PHC).
tip.all_good: Your answers look healthy. Keep eating whole foods, staying active and sleeping well.
models.intro: Both models were tested on people they never saw during training. The risk cut-off of each is tuned so that about 8 in 10 people with diabetes are flagged — for screening, a false alarm costs one blood test, but a missed case can cost years of health.
models.survey_data: Trained on the CDC BRFSS health survey: {n} US adults, {prev} of whom had diabetes or prediabetes. Uses 14 self-reported answers, no lab tests.
models.clinical_data: Trained on the Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset: {n} women aged 21+, {prev} of whom had diabetes. Uses 8 measurements, including a 2-hour glucose test.
models.method: **Model:** calibrated {model}, chosen by cross-validation and evaluated once on {n_test} held-out people.
models.sensitivity_help: Share of people with diabetes who are flagged.
models.specificity_help: Share of healthy people correctly cleared.
models.threshold: The risk cut-off is **{t}** instead of the usual 50%, so that about {target} of people with diabetes are flagged. At 50% the model would miss {missed} of them.
models.charts: Charts: feature importance, ROC curve, confusion matrix, calibration, model comparison
fig.confusion_matrix: Confusion matrix at the screening cut-off
about.body:
**Why this matters.** About 101 million Indians have diabetes and 136 million have prediabetes (ICMR-INDIAB, 2023). Many are diagnosed late, especially in rural and low-income areas, because tests cost money and labs are far away. A quick screen helps health workers decide who needs a blood test first.

**Two checks.**
- **Quick check** — 14 everyday questions, no lab test. Built for self-checks and ASHA/health-camp screening.
- **Detailed check** — uses lab readings such as a 2-hour glucose test, for people who already have reports.

**Limitations.**
- The quick-check model learned from US adults and the detailed model from women of Pima heritage; neither has been validated on Indian patients yet. South Asians tend to develop diabetes at a lower BMI, so the estimates may be too low.
- The quick-check result covers diabetes *or* prediabetes, as self-reported in the survey.
- Both should be re-trained on local data before real clinical use.

**Languages.** English, हिन्दी and ಕನ್ನಡ. Share a link ending in `?lang=hi` or `?lang=kn` to open the app directly in that language.
